title: ARWP Page Semantics Profile
scope: Source-backed page-type, structured-data, identity, offer/service, event and source-routing rules for repository agents preparing public websites.

entityGraph.idPolicy: Use stable absolute canonical URLs and stable fragments when useful (#website, #software, #person, #service-*); reuse the same @id for the same entity.
entityGraph.sameAs: Only unambiguous identity aliases, never topical/category links.

rules.rule: Choose markup after page classification. Properties must be accurate and supported by visible first-party content; fewer complete/accurate properties beat large inaccurate graphs.
Use one coherent WebSite identity and one real publisher Person/Organization identity; use the most specific organization subtype when it genuinely applies.
Keep visible authorship, Article-family author Person/Organization, author.url and real ProfilePage identity consistent. Never invent biography or credentials.
Keep visible Published/Updated labels, datePublished/dateModified and sitemap lastmod truthful; do not churn freshness timestamps on every build.

When targeting Google's event experience, each real event needs a unique useful leaf URL focused on one event; visible name/start/location must match Event markup. Google currently requires events eligible for its event experience to be bookable by the general public and held at a physical location.

Use Schema.org PublicationEvent for a real publication/release occurrence when that event itself has user or provenance value. Do not present an online software/content publication event as Google event-rich-result eligible when it lacks the required public physical event characteristics.

Use Dataset for dataset-shaped assets and preserve creator/publisher, identifier, license, distribution and provenance when known; citation is for related publications, not the dataset's own identity.
Canonical tags, internal links and sitemap inventory should converge on intended canonical URLs; keep redirects, noindex and accidental duplicate variants out of the canonical sitemap.
Use separate localized URLs and one maintainable hreflang mechanism with reciprocal plus self references. HTML, headers and sitemap are alternatives, not stackable ranking layers.
Treat nosnippet, max-snippet, data-nosnippet and max-image-preview as intentional publisher controls; surface restrictive settings rather than silently applying them.
Use DefinedTerm and DefinedTermSet for stable term identity, definitions and membership when the site has a genuine vocabulary; this is semantic graphing, not a Google rich-result promise.

Use Service and OfferCatalog when a page genuinely describes services or accessible capabilities. Keep provider, service URLs and offer facts truthful. Schema.org service semantics are not by themselves a Google Search rich-result entitlement.

SoftwareApplication can describe a real software surface, but Google's software-app rich result has additional eligibility requirements: name and offers.price plus a genuine rating or review. For free software, offers.price may be 0. Never fabricate ratings or reviews to satisfy eligibility.
Use visible, useful hierarchy and BreadcrumbList where it reflects a real user navigation path. Do not create fake parent pages only to support breadcrumb markup.

rules.applies: evergreen content with repository/agent source needs
rules.rule: Do not publish a same-host Markdown duplicate of every canonical HTML page as an SEO tactic. Google says llms.txt is not needed for Search and does not affect rankings; duplicate formats can create canonicalization work. Prefer one canonical indexable HTML URL and, when useful, keep Markdown as a repository-only authoring/agent source linked through a machine page manifest.
Remove obsolete feature-only markup when it has no semantic value. Do not add universal FAQ/HowTo, fake reviews/ratings/offers, or SearchAction solely for the retired Google sitelinks search box.

antiPatterns: machine-only facts absent from visible content
SearchAction only for retired sitelinks search box
FAQPage/HowTo added universally for rich-result hopes
thin author/event/glossary pages created only for bots
public same-host Markdown clones of every canonical HTML page
fake software reviews or ratings added to satisfy rich-result requirements
online publication/release milestones marketed as Google physical event rich-result candidates
